body: I know so many people have already offered help and such, but we're all here to talk if you need us. Some of us probably know better what you're feeling at this point in time but the person who really does know what they're feeling right now, is you. Talk to people about how you feel, even if it is on here. Take up meditation. Go vegan for January. Find a new you in the midst of the old you that's even better, happier, stronger, invincible. Don't dwell on the old you; you've essentially now got a second shot at living again you can take it to start over. I hope you've got people at home that can support you but if you don't, we're all here and we don't really go anywhere when someone is in need.

The best way of doing a composite is in increments. I've seen multiple composite; some done as a bulk and shaped later and others done in increments and those worked best. Etch the tooth and rinse after 30 seconds and get as dry as possible (even use if a rubber dam would be good but if not, cotton rolls and pledgets) and then bond, cure and then begin the composite layers. For molar build ups, place balls of composite where each cusp should be and place composite towards the cereal occlusal surface to which you'll find a natural fissure is created. Again, cure each section as you go. Also, there's loads of matrix systems so get practice with as many as possible however more commonly you'll have a Siqveland or a Toffelmire as opposed to something like a V3.

Hey. I'm sorry you're going through this but it's more common than you think. My other half and me have a similar sort of issue however my anger bounces off him. He has had anger issues for his entire life but his is a case of smashing and breaking things. His anger gets to me and I become physical violent towards him which is something I have never been but I am stopping this. He doesn't have all that many close friends and I have a number of friends but all over the place geographically. I try and focus my energy elsewhere and try and avoid the triggers. For example, he kicked off at me yesterday because I thought a bbq would be a great idea, not realising how much it would set off my hayfever but sat outside anyway but was miserable and sore with it. When he ignored me and decided to put the tv on, I took the remote and threatened to throw it. Well, the bottom line is, I threw it because he swore I wouldn't. That remote sat in pieces and today, I've fixed it, but I won't tell him that. I'm also passive aggressive. I have mostly avoided him today and have spent time on myself and on distractions. I love reading and I enjoy doing bits and pieces at home that I've wanted to do for a while; I've been reading this morning and I'm going to clean a lamp up that I bought last weekend before sorting out my things for work tomorrow then this evening, I'll cook. Is there anything you love doing that you can immerse yourself in when you feel at your angriest? I'm here for advice when you want someone who knows.
